reading.text:
UNIT def:LevyStochCalc.Poisson.naturalFiltration
Standing setting (paper section 2, intro (eq:mvfbsdej), section 3 solution space, section 4,
appendix A): (Omega, F, (F_t), P) satisfying the usual conditions, horizon T > 0; a d-dim
Brownian motion W and an independent Poisson random measure N on R_+ x E with intensity
dt nu(de), nu sigma-finite on a countably generated (E, calE); (F_t) is the usual augmentation
of the filtration generated by W, N and an independent initial sigma-field F_0. The compensated
measure is Ntilde(dt,de) = N(dt,de) - dt nu(de). Integrands U of the Poisson integral are
predictable: P (x) calE-measurable, P the predictable sigma-field on Omega x [0,T]
(eq:fubiniiso), with E int_0^T ||U_t||^2_{L2(nu)} dt < infinity (the space H^2_N). The
integral int_0^t int_E U_s(e) Ntilde(ds,de) is the standard L2 (Ito-Levy) compensated-Poisson
integral: an L2 martingale, cadlag, with the isometry E|int_0^t int U dNtilde|^2 =
E int_0^t ||U_s||^2 ds (used in Lemma 4.1 "true L2-martingales by the Ito and
compensated-Poisson isometries"), jumps Delta = U_s(e) at atoms (s,e) of N, and for integrands
in L1(dP dt nu) the integral splits as int U dN - int U nu ds (eq:compid, eq:zeromean).
Progressive measurability is used for the coefficient processes b, sigma, f and the forcings
q^b, q^sigma, q^f (eq:coefmeas, section 4); predictability (P (x) calE) for h and q^h.

Reading.
Paper notion: "the filtration generated by W, N and an independent initial sigma-field F_0",
before augmentation. A definition named Poisson.naturalFiltration presumably is the natural
filtration of the Poisson random measure N (the N-part of that generating family, possibly
joined with W or F_0 elsewhere): F^N_t = sigma(N(A) : A measurable subset of [0,t] x E)
(equivalently generated by N((s,u] x B), u <= t, B in calE, or B of finite nu-mass: these
generate the same sigma-algebra because nu is sigma-finite and N((s,u] x B) is the increasing
limit of N((s,u] x B_k)). Faithful Lean: for each t in the time domain, the sigma-algebra
generated by the [0,infinity]-valued random variables omega -> N(omega)(A), A measurable
subset of [0,t] x E (or the cells above), as a Mathlib Filtration (monotone, contained in the
ambient sigma-algebra; the latter requires measurability of these maps, provided by the PRM).
Inclusion or exclusion of the time 0 slice is harmless (N({0} x E) = 0 a.s.). If it also
includes W and/or F_0 it is the paper's generating filtration itself; then it must be generated
by W_s (s <= t), N on [0,t] x E, and F_0. No augmentation at this stage.

comparison.text:
Lean (LevyStochCalc/Poisson/NaturalFiltration.lean): naturalFiltration N : Filtration R m0 with
seq t = sup over measurable C subset of Iic t x univ of comap (omega -> N omega C) (Borel on
ENNReal); mono' and le' proved (le' from measurable_eval).
Comparison with the locked reading: this is the natural filtration of N alone,
F^N_t = sigma(N(A) : A measurable subset of (-inf,t] x E), as a Mathlib Filtration (monotone,
inside the ambient sigma-algebra). It includes all measurable regions and all mark sets
(equivalent to generating by cells with finite nu-mass, as the reading noted). Representation
choices: (1) the time axis is R, so the regions include negative times and the time-0 slice; N
vanishes a.s. there (intensity 0, including {0} x E since 0 * top = 0), so these generators add
only null/conull events - harmless; (2) it does not include W or F_0 (those are joined elsewhere
in the library's joint filtration), consistent with the name and with the reading's first
option; (3) no augmentation, as the reading required.

verdict.detail:
Representation choices: (1) time axis R: the generating regions include negative times and the
time-0 slice, where N vanishes a.s. (intensity 0, with 0 * top = 0), so these generators add only
null/conull events; (2) it is the natural filtration of N alone - W and F_0 are joined in the
library's joint filtration - and it is not augmented, matching the paper's generating family
before augmentation; (3) all measurable regions and mark sets are used as generators, which gives
the same sigma-algebra as finite-mass cells since nu is sigma-finite.

author_review.disagreements:
Minor, classification only: the author records "faithful"; I record "faithful with
representation choices" (time axis R: the generators include negative-time regions and the time-0
slice, where N vanishes a.s.; it is the natural filtration of N alone, W and F_0 being joined
elsewhere). Harmless; no substantive disagreement.
